# Motion Design Instructions

- Assign motion density per section: Level 0 through Level 5. Do not use density
  as a quota.
- Each scene needs one primary message and primary, secondary, and ambient motion
  roles.
- Use design tokens for color, type, spacing, safe zones, duration, easing,
  distance, stagger, blur, scale, transitions, camera, and reduced motion.
- Use kinetic typography only when movement adds meaning, rhythm, emphasis, or
  structure. Keep captions separate unless intentionally unified.
- Reveal diagrams, processes, and mind maps progressively with stable orientation
  anchors.
- Preserve data values, units, baselines, labels, order, geography, chronology,
  UI behavior, and source attribution.
- Use 3D, shaders, particles, and advanced effects only when they improve the
  message or identity and render cost/QC time is budgeted.
- Prefer transform and opacity for frequent browser motion; avoid decorative
  camera movement, unique transitions for every scene, and visual noise behind
  text or evidence.
